scope: read-only source/diff review; no Python module imports, tests, child processes or renderer/GPU executions
result: No concrete ownership/deadline/cleanup regression found in the three helper deltas. Two precision findings and one incidental host-parser mismatch sent to author.
checks: Default empty pass_fds keeps descriptors closed; default wide waiting grammar/release marker/forbidden set is unchanged.
Both launcher layers validate at most one integer fd>=3 and preserve it with explicit pass_fds.
AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, SO_ACCEPTCONN, loopback address and nonzero port are checked; valid socket wrapper detaches rather than closing caller fd.
Timing launcher browser Popen uses close_fds=True without pass_fds; listener is not inherited by the browser.
Existing sole-waiter WAITID WNOWAIT ownership, signals before reap, subreaper adoption, cancellation, original timeout, bounded output/draining and cleanup status remain unchanged.
Wide delayed response still requires owned resize plus latest waiting-size evidence, and fully drains pre-release diagnostic bytes before opening the gate.

findings.text: validate_listener_fds calls accepted sockets TCP but does not check socket protocol; an AF_INET listening non-TCP SOCK_STREAM socket could meet current predicate. Actual caller creates TCP.
bridge_supervisor module header still says never import into running host, while run_supervised intentionally imports its inert descriptor validation helper.
At read time native_raster_timing_host.validate_report required integer for CPU cleanup_ns, but presenter deliberately reports None for that unreached CPU phase; notified script before execution.
